subject: astronomy

items.q: What is a black hole's event horizon?
items.correct: The boundary beyond which not even light can escape.
items.misconception: The visible 'edge' of the black hole.
items.random_wrong: A literal horizon you can walk to.
items.why: Students picture a surface. The event horizon is a mathematical BOUNDARY - nothing is physically there. Once inside, escape requires faster-than-light speed, which is impossible.

items.q: What was the first galaxy whose central black hole was imaged by the EHT?
items.why: Correct answer: M87. “Andromeda” sounds right because it borrows the language of the topic — but it fails this question. Re-read the notes on why.

items.q: Where is most of the energy of an active galaxy produced?
items.correct: Accretion disc around the central black hole
items.why: It's Accretion disc around the central black hole. “Halo of old stars” is the classic near-miss here; knowing why it's wrong is worth as much as knowing the right answer.

items.q: In what year was the first direct image of a black hole released?
items.why: Exact answer: 2019. Estimation gets you near it; only the anchored number survives the exam hall.
